stack.singlePhysicalHost: Controllers, PostgreSQL, MinIO, Caddy, the remote workers, their sandbox containers, the fixture target and the load generator all share one machine and one Docker daemon; no cross-host network or hardware was measured.
stack.clientTransport: HTTPS to Caddy on loopback (tls internal), round robin over both controllers; TLS termination and the proxy hop are included
stack.authentication: bearer API tokens; runner principals admit, the owner reads
stack.storage: MinIO with TLS, bind-mounted local directory, evidence bucket

target.note: The tool has no target option and never sends load to anything but this fixture.

stack.observation: State is read with docker compose exec psql and the filesystem, not through the load generator's event loop

method.load: closed loop: each in-flight slot admits a Run, waits until it is completed and starts the next; admission retries reuse the idempotency key
method.percentileRule: p50 and p90 from n >= 1; p95 only from n >= 100, p99 only from n >= 500; otherwise null with the reason in "withheld"
method.runTimeSource: wall time = Run created_at to the last Attempt's ended_at; phases from attempt.timing events (monotonic); client-observed time adds the 500 ms poll interval
method.sizing: requiredSlots ≈ arrivalRate × meanServiceTime / 0.7 is an estimate (OPS-034), not a guarantee

isolation.statement: No hostile multi-tenant test was run and no isolation promise follows from these numbers. Workspace isolation is an authorization and row-level-security boundary inside one process and one database, and a container is not a hostile multi-tenant boundary on its own: a tenant that can run arbitrary code needs a separate host or VM boundary.

notMeasured: More than one physical host: cross-host latency, clock skew and partial or asymmetric partitions.
Hostile multi-tenant behaviour and cross-tenant fairness under attack.
Artifacts larger than a few KiB (the 64 MiB publication target).
Browser, terminal and Python runners; only the HTTP runner against a fixed-delay target was loaded.
S3 implementations other than the pinned MinIO; AWS S3 behaviour and latency.
Queue start lag with every slot busy (the soak keeps slots available by design).
Any percentile whose n is below the gate (see each "withheld").
Backup, restore and retention under load.
limitations: One physical host: every component competes for the same CPU, memory, disk and Docker daemon, and the load generator is one of them.
The partition is emulated by freezing the worker process (SIGSTOP), which stops its heartbeats and calls but not its sandbox container; a partial partition is not exercised.
The duplicate-execution check assumes the fixture sees one request per Attempt, as the benchmark plan sends.
Every authenticated request writes an audit row, including the load generator's 500 ms Run polling, so database growth per Run includes that polling.
Drift slopes cover one window and exclude the first 20%; they do not prove the absence of a slower leak.
Admissions are limited by the per-principal (20 burst, 1/s) and per-tenant (200 burst, 20/s) budgets, so sustained admission cannot exceed about 20 per second whatever the controllers could do.
